So here's the Math
Imagine Mr. Musk (Tesla wale), an FII, invested ₹100 in India a year ago when $1 = ₹82. His investment grows 10%, so now it’s worth ₹110. Sounds good, right?

But here’s the catch — the rupee depreciated during this time, and now $1 = ₹88. So when he converts his ₹110 back to dollars, he only gets $1.25. Basically, his 10% gain in rupees shrunk to just 2.5% in dollars.

And wait — there's 20% long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax too. So after paying ₹2 as tax, he’s left with ₹108, which converts to just $1.2.

Now compare this to if he had just parked his money in U.S. Treasury bonds that gave around 5% return — without any currency risk or tax headache.

So from Mr. Musk’s point of view — he took the risk, faced currency depreciation, paid taxes, and ended up with a lower dollar return than if he had just stayed home and invested in U.S. bonds.

That’s exactly why FIIs are pulling out  - Put High LTCG on top and you have a recipe for disaster

verbatim_text:
Apne audience ko samjhaiye ki SIP ka duration matter karta hai. 
1) nifty 50 index ya large cap 5-6+ years 
2) flexicap 7+ years kyunki thoda S+M cap hota hai, mostly large cap allocation
3) small, mid, multicap etc 10+ years ke liye hota hai.
Covid ke baad wala returns sirf illusion thha. Majaal nhi hai ki long term returns koi fund 20% se jyada de de.

Nifty 50- 12%
Flexicap- 13-14%
Large and midcap 14-15%
Midcap - 15-16%
Small cap 17-18%
Multicap 15-16%
Realistic target rakhiye aur allocation sahi rakhe.
Nifty 50 index plus flexicap 50-60%
Mid and small cap 40-50% 
Jyada risk lene se koi faayda nhi, market crash hone par insaan ko aukaat ka pata chalta hai.
Issliye convenient amount se SIP start kijiye, shuruaat me HDFC BAF se start karna better hai. Yahi portfolio ko sambhalega.
